newsitem.title: JAPAN: JM's Russia PGM stock report seen bullish - traders.
newsitem.headline: JM's Russia PGM stock report seen bullish - traders.

text.p: A Johnson Matthey Plc report saying that Russian platinum group metals (PGM) stocks are expected to run down will be bullish for world PGM prices, Japanese traders said on Tuesday.

Russian inventories of platinum could run out within a year and its palladium stocks could be depleted early in the next century, Jeremy Coombes, Johnson Matthey's general manager, said in London on Monday.

"It is rather shocking that Russian platinum stocks would dry out in about one year, although we have suspected the capacity of Russian platinum stocks is limited," one senior trader at a trading house said.
"Even if South Africa can increase production of PGM, only South Africa could not be enough for filling the shortage. So, the factor would be bullish for PGM prices," the trader said.
Another trader echoed the views, saying that the comments by Johnson Matthey, the world's largest refiner of PGM, have cast an additional cloud over Russian supplies.
"Maybe South Africa could increase platinum output to fill the gap. But it would be risky to depend on only one country for metal supplies, so supply fears may grow," the trader said.
The trader said the drawdown of Russian palladium stocks would have greater effects on palladium, as Russia supplies more than 60 percent of the metal to the world.
Japanese traders said Johnson Matthey's view on demand/supply PGM situations in 1996 were within their expectations and came as little surprise to the market.

The prolonged suspension of Russian PGM exports since the beginning of this year has hit the Japanese palladium market, but platinum prices have not been as affected by the Russian export halts, as South Africa is able to fill the shortage.

Traders added there has been no progress in the Japan-Russian PGM export contract talks for 1997 so far after Almazjuvelirexport, the Russian PGM marketing agency, informed Japanese clients last week that Russian sales would resume soon.

Traders agreed with JM's views that palladium prices remain vulnerable, saying the prolonged suspension of Russian PGM supplies and the unpredictablity of Russian sales levels when they are resumed could result in significant excursions above and below the trading range for palladium.
The JM report predicted palladium prices would move within a range between 120 and 160 dollars an ounce this year.
